To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
estrogen-induced implantation in the rat requires formation of a catechol.
the catechol estradiols 2-OH-E2 and 4-OH-E2 induce implantation in the rat.

1) estradiol-2, 4-dimethyl ether (2,4-ME2-E2), a compound that cannot be metabolized to catechol estrogens, does not initiate implantation of the rat embryo; and, 2) estradiol, a catechol estrogen, does induce implantation of rat embryos.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the catechol metabolites of estrogen in the induction of implantation of the blastocyst in the uterus.
the mechanisms of estrogen action.
the mechanism of action of estradiol-178 (E2), a hormone that is essential for implant-ation and maintenance of pregnancy in the rat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the formation of catecholestradiols is not essential for estrogen-induced implantation in the rat.
the catechol estrogens are not essential for estrogen action in implantation.
the catechol estrogen 2-hydroxyestrone (2-OHE1) is the most potent estrogen in the rat uterus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
catechol estradiols can induce implantation in a progesteronedependent manner, and that catechol formation may be essential for this effect.
estrogen-induced implantation is dependent upon the formation of catechols.
the catechol metabolites of estrogen are important in mediating implantation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the catechol estrogen, 2-OH E2 is a potent estrogen that is able to induce implantation in the progesterone-pretreated rat.
the estrogen receptor (ER) can be activated by catechol estradiols and that the activation is dependent on the catechol structure.
the catechol estrogen 2-OH-E2 can induce implantation in the rat, but the fluorinated analogs 2-F1-2 and 4-F1-2 cannot, even though the latter are as potent as estradiol-178 (E2) in the rat uterus.
